questions.q: In the prompt 'pi@raspberrypi:~$', what does the tilde (~) tell you?
choices: You are logged in as the root administrator
You are currently in your personal home folder
The machine is connected to the network
The terminal is waiting for a sudo password
questions.explain: The tilde (~) is a shortcut that always means 'your home folder' (e.g. /home/pi). Root access is indicated by a # sign instead of $ at the end of the prompt — not by the tilde.

questions.q: You want to save a file and exit the nano editor. Which sequence of key presses does this correctly?
choices: Ctrl + S, then Ctrl + Q
Ctrl + W, then Enter
Esc, then type :wq and Enter
Ctrl + O, then Enter, then Ctrl + X
questions.explain: In nano, Ctrl + O writes (saves) the file — press Enter to confirm the filename — then Ctrl + X exits. Ctrl + S and :wq are shortcuts from other programs (Windows apps and Vim respectively), not nano.

questions.q: Which command would you use to copy a folder and everything inside it?
choices: cp myfolder/ backup/
cp -r myfolder/ backup/
mv myfolder/ backup/
mkdir -p backup/ myfolder/
questions.explain: The -r flag (recursive) is required when copying a folder with cp. Without it, cp refuses to copy directories. mv would move rather than copy, and mkdir only creates new empty folders.

questions.q: What happens when you run 'rm backup.txt' on Raspberry Pi OS?
choices: The file is moved to a Recycle Bin and can be restored
The terminal asks 'are you sure?' before deleting
The file is permanently deleted with no undo
The command fails unless you add sudo first
questions.explain: The rm command permanently deletes files with no Recycle Bin, no undo, and no confirmation prompt by default. You can add the -i flag to make it ask before each deletion, but this is not the default behaviour.

questions.q: You run 'ls /usr/bin | grep python'. What does the pipe (|) do here?
choices: It saves the output of ls to a file called grep
It runs ls and grep at the same time in parallel
It sends the output of ls directly into grep as its input, so grep can filter it
It tells ls to only list files whose names contain 'python'
questions.explain: The pipe (|) connects two commands: the output that ls would normally print to the screen is instead handed to grep as input. grep then filters that list and prints only the lines containing 'python'.
